title: Assuring the emotional and cultural intelligence of intelligent software systems
findings: The paper argues that intelligent systems can perpetuate discrimination by misunderstanding cultural differences. It provides the way people 'pray' as a single example of a cultural dimension that, if misinterpreted, can lead to bias. The paper does not contain empirical findings about religion but proposes developing 'Emotional and Cultural Intelligence (ECI)' requirements to build fairer systems.
references: B. Belle, A., Sutherland, C., Adesina, O. O., Kpodjedo, S., Ojong, N., & Cole, L. (2023). Bolstering the Persistence of Black Students in Undergraduate Computer Science Programs: A Systematic Mapping Study. ACM Transactions on Computing Education.
G. Rodríguez-Pérez, R. Nadri, and M. Nagappan. 2021. Perceived diversity in software engineering: A systematic literature review. Empirical Software Engineering 26, 5 (2021), 1–38
Hofstede, G. (2011). National cultures, organizational cultures, and the role of management. Values and Ethics for the 21st Century. Madrid: BBVA, 459-81.

Paulo Coehlo's Intercultural dialogue blog. https://paulocoelhoblog.com/2015/03/13/intercultural-dialogue/ [Accessed in November 2023].
measurement_description: The paper does not present a benchmark, but proposes a new type of non-functional requirement called 'ECI (emotional and cultural intelligence)' to assure against socio-cultural discrimination. Religious practice ('how people...pray') is mentioned once as an example of a cultural expression that could be misinterpreted by AI, but it is not a measured component.
